(but then it is a question how to pass the arguments between different implementations... maybe this will be sorted in specific precompile implementations in each client seems that it requires attention if the `gnark` code is indeed conformant then it sounds like the geth code may be out of date wrt the latest spec -- <@!211091239112671234> do you have a link to what i think is the `bls12381` package you are referencing (or whatever they mean by "geth code")? and while there may have been some minor spec updates to the BLS cryptosystem, they shouldn't really affect the BLS12-381 arithmetic that we want to get into the EVM a la EIP-2537 i also lean towards the "shanghai should be a pressure-release valve fork" camp (from today's call) but it would be great to see something like 2537 soon as it unlocks a lot of interesting new use cases (and is more or less required for sharding) Would withdrawals replace the deposit contract? If so, doing 2537 in conjunction would allow us to improve the deposit contract as well, right? i'm assuming it is just the `bls12381` package in geth today yes i don't think we want to touch the deposit contract without very good reason there is some WIP work on withdrawals here: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2759 basic idea is to make a "withdrawals root" (like the "deposit root" in the deposit contract today) and expose that to the evm How would we unlock the ETH from the deposit contract? if we do the "change of credentials" operation referenced in that PR then we don't need userspace BLS math Or would we do an invalid state transition on every withdrawal? the eth can stay in the deposit contract that eth is "burned" The ETH in the deposit contract isn't enough: there are also validator rewards to account for like if you sent eth to `0x0` define "invalid" valid is just the rules of the protocol if you have a sink into the beacon chain (the dpeosit contract) and a pull out of it -- some withdrawal receipts root -- that is functionally equivalent to a deposit/withdrawal contract that did both functions together Hmm, It would mean that we would increase the money supply by 32 + validator rewards ETH on every withdrawal. Just think it is not easy to explain that to the general audience That's already the case, though! the "money supply" is less the value in the deposit contract yeah, as <@!552133098075193354> mentions, you can already have that issue if you choose to frame it that way the "money supply" is beacon-chain validator balances plus EL balances minus deposit contract balance if this is really a concern, just write down the algorithm and expose the "supply" as a json rpc endpoint to make the bitcoiners happy I *really* don't think it's worth the consensus and development complexity to try to make this look too clean because the bitcoiners will complain Opened an Ethereum Magicians thread so we can bikeshed the EL naming for the merge client releases: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/el-merge-client-release-naming/7928 🤔 1. As long as 66%+ of validators are one client, all clients will refuse to finalize until the number drops below 66%. imho a very clear option is Paris https://twitter.com/evan_van_ness/status/1479521576404062212

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: <@!489256758989029405> re your question about bls - "did it age since then?". I'm not sure, but someone better at crypto than me can maybe tell me -- is this a significant change? https://github.com/ConsenSys/gnark-crypto/issues/103

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content: Something about how infinity is represented which seemingly has changed... ???

excerpts.author: tkstanczak
excerpts.content: this may be just the way you invoke the code based on the tone of their answer - seems that if you remain in the same implementation then all is good? (but then it is a question how to pass the arguments between different implementations...

excerpts.author: tkstanczak
excerpts.content: maybe this will be sorted in specific precompile implementations in each client

excerpts.author: tkstanczak
excerpts.content: seems that it requires attention

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: if the `gnark` code is indeed conformant then it sounds like the geth code may be out of date wrt the latest spec -- <@!211091239112671234> do you have a link to what i think is the `bls12381` package you are referencing (or whatever they mean by "geth code")?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: and while there may have been some minor spec updates to the BLS cryptosystem, they shouldn't really affect the BLS12-381 arithmetic that we want to get into the EVM a la EIP-2537

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: i also lean towards the "shanghai should be a pressure-release valve fork" camp (from today's call) but it would be great to see something like 2537 soon as it unlocks a lot of interesting new use cases (and is more or less required for sharding)

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content:
Would withdrawals replace the deposit contract?
If so, doing 2537 in conjunction would allow us to improve the deposit contract as well, right?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: i'm assuming it is just the `bls12381` package in geth today

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: yes

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: i don't think we want to touch the deposit contract without very good reason

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: there is some WIP work on withdrawals here: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2759

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: basic idea is to make a "withdrawals root" (like the "deposit root" in the deposit contract today) and expose that to the evm

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: How would we unlock the ETH from the deposit contract?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: if we do the "change of credentials" operation referenced in that PR then we don't need userspace BLS math

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Or would we do an invalid state transition on every withdrawal?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: the eth can stay in the deposit contract

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: that eth is "burned"

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: The ETH in the deposit contract isn't enough: there are also validator rewards to account for

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: like if you sent eth to `0x0`

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: define "invalid"

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: valid is just the rules of the protocol

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: if you have a sink into the beacon chain (the dpeosit contract) and a pull out of it -- some withdrawal receipts root -- that is functionally equivalent to a deposit/withdrawal contract that did both functions together

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content:
Hmm, It would mean that we would increase the money supply by 32 + validator rewards ETH on every withdrawal.
Just think it is not easy to explain that to the general audience

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: That's already the case, though!

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: the "money supply" is less the value in the deposit contract

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: yeah, as <@!552133098075193354> mentions, you can already have that issue if you choose to frame it that way

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: the "money supply" is beacon-chain validator balances plus EL  balances minus deposit contract balance

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: if this is really a concern, just write down the algorithm and expose the "supply" as a json rpc endpoint to make the bitcoiners happy

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: I *really* don't think it's worth the consensus and development complexity to try to make this look too clean because the bitcoiners will complain

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: Opened an Ethereum Magicians thread so we can bikeshed the EL naming for the merge client releases: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/el-merge-client-release-naming/7928

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content:
🤔
1. Validators include their client (Lighthouse, Teku, Prysm, etc.) in their validation.
2. As long as 66%+ of validators are one client, all clients will refuse to finalize until the number drops below 66%.
